beats.text: A one minute pose was said to change your hormones.
beats.note: Dana Carney, Amy Cuddy and Andy Yap reported higher testosterone and lower cortisol after a high power pose.

beats.context: The final sample of the original study, after five exclusions.

beats.text: A larger replication found no hormone effect.
beats.note: Ranehill and colleagues used 200 people, 98 women and 102 men, and held the poses for three minutes. Testosterone, cortisol and risk taking did not change significantly.

beats.text: People still said they felt more powerful.
beats.note: That self reported feeling was the one result the replication confirmed.

beats.name: Dana Carney
beats.role: The lead author of the 2010 study. She said she does not believe the power pose effects are real, and listed flaws including checking the result while running the study in batches.

beats.text: The feeling held up. The hormone claim did not.

beats.line: A small study is a question, not an answer.
